Hyperrealistic cinematic documentary, indistinguishable from real footage. Vertical 9:16 aspect ratio. One continuous 30-second take, one uninterrupted shot, no cuts, no edits, unstabilized handheld camera, no stabilization whatsoever, shot on Sony VENICE 2 with ZEISS Supreme Prime lenses, 8.6K full-frame sensor, 16 stops of dynamic range, dual native ISO 800/3200, wide color gamut exceeding BT.2020, precise color reproduction, natural skin tones, cool neutral tones, clean sharp image, high detail, modern digital look, minimal fine film-like grain instead of electronic noise, smooth creamy bokeh with natural fall-off, round highlights in out-of-focus areas, no busy background rendering, slight chromatic aberration at the edges, natural vignetting, soft highlight roll-off. The lens coating controls light — when sunlight hits the glass, the flare is soft and restrained, never washing out the image. Contrast stays high even in backlight. Light refracts gently across the lens surface, creating a subtle, controlled glow, not a harsh flare. Natural exposure shifts, auto-exposure jumps when the camera turns from bright sky to darker ground, brief focus hunting during fast movements, manual autofocus that breathes and occasionally misses, then catches up, horizon slightly tilted, camera hand repositioning, breathing audible and visible in the frame rhythm. Real human behavior, no staged acting, natural micro-expressions, constant subtle movement. All dialogue in clear, native Russian, perfect pronunciation, natural intonation, as spoken by native Russian speakers. No accent, no foreign inflection, no robotic delivery.

The camera is handheld, unstabilized. The operator is never visible in frame — no hands, no body, no face. Every mention of the operator refers only to the behavior of the camera: when the operator moves, the frame moves; when the operator breathes, the camera shakes slightly; when the operator ducks or steps back, the camera drops or pulls back. The audience only sees what the camera sees.

Location: exactly as in <<<image_1>>> and <<<image_2>>> — the embankment of the Moskva River near the parking area, with a distant view of Moscow State University. Take only the location itself: no people, no poses from the references. Ignore any people present. Use only the space, architecture, ground, parapet, water, sky, and weather. The rain has just stopped, the sun is coming out. Wet asphalt, puddles reflecting the sky and the building. The parapet glistens. Moisture in the air. Sunlight breaks through the clouds in soft rays, occasional lens flares. Clouds move slowly, light shifts across the scene, shadows drift. No trees, no leaves on the asphalt. A light wind blows across the embankment — it moves hair, flutters clothes, ripples puddles slightly, keeps the air alive.

Alexander, matching <<<image_5>>>, stands near the main pickup from <<<image_7>>>. He holds the Sony VENICE 2 from <<<image_3>>> in his hands. John, matching <<<image_6>>>, stands beside him, holding an open case with the ZEISS Supreme Prime lenses from <<<image_4>>>. The dent from a previous impact is visible on the truck's side panel. Wet handprints on the metal. Condensation drips from the exhaust pipe. The truck's reflection ripples in the puddle below. Alexander turns to the camera and says in clear, native Russian, perfect pronunciation, natural intonation: «Сейчас мы снимаем на Sony VENICE 2 с объективами ZEISS Supreme Prime.» He speaks directly to the camera, calm, confident. The wind moves his damp hair and clothes. A glare from the puddle briefly hits his face.

As soon as he finishes the line, Alexander casually tosses the camera out of frame, to the side. Off-screen, a young reddish-haired assistant in glasses catches it — just barely, fumbling, catching it at the last second, a look of surprise on his face. The camera does not linger on him — the frame stays on Alexander. John sets the open lens case down on the wet asphalt.

Then, without warning, John drops into a fighting stance — a classic Bruce Lee pose. He taps his nose lightly with one finger, bounces on his feet, a faint smile of enjoyment on his face. Alexander shifts into a mixed martial arts stance. They start sparring — real, gritty, not always clean. John moves like Bruce Lee: precise, fast, controlled. Alexander moves like an MMA fighter: grounded, heavy, powerful. Both are damp from the rain, hair slightly wet, clothes clinging lightly to their bodies, sweat on their skin. They exchange kicks and punches on the wet asphalt, slipping slightly, catching balance. Some punches miss, some are blocked. At one point they clinch — pushing, shoving, unable to break apart, breathing hard in each other's faces. Then they separate, circle, catch their breath. Water splashes under their feet with each step. Wet footprints stay on the ground. Their breath is short and audible. When a punch lands, one of them exhales sharply, the other grimaces briefly, then recovers. A red mark appears on Alexander's cheekbone. John's lip is split — he wipes it, looks at his finger, smirks. Alexander rotates his shoulder after a block, checking it. The wind moves their damp hair and clothes as they fight, adding constant subtle motion to every frame.

Alexander tries to keep talking through the fight, explaining, but his words break up between breaths and dodges. He says in clear, native Russian, perfect pronunciation, natural intonation: «Обратите внимание — качество изображения отличается от прошлого, потому что прошлое было снято на ARRI Alexa 35.» He blocks a punch mid-sentence, keeps going. He says in clear, native Russian, perfect pronunciation, natural intonation: «Sony даёт холодные, нейтральные и точные тона. Современная, чистая картинка — без плёночной мягкости.» He dodges a kick, stumbles, recovers. He says in clear, native Russian, perfect pronunciation, natural intonation: «Касательно объектива. Вы можете заметить, что здесь блики ведут себя по-другому. Специальное покрытие объективов не позволяет бликам перекрывать всё изображение и терять контрастность.»

The camera moves dynamically — running around the fighters, circling, ducking, crouching low when they close in, stepping closer, pulling back, dropping low and shooting upward, tilting the horizon slightly. The frame breathes with every move. When a punch flies too close, the camera jerks back, the frame drops, the focus slips, then recovers. There is a brief exhale of relief when it misses. The camera stumbles on a curb, the horizon tilts badly, then corrects. Breathing is heavy, sometimes through the mouth, sometimes through the nose. At one point, when the camera moves past the truck, the operator's faint reflection briefly appears in the wet body panel — a dark silhouette with the camera, gone in a split second. No one reacts. The reflection also ripples in the puddle below. The camera does not linger on it.

At one point, John is pushed back hard and slams into the side of the pickup, his back hitting the metal with a dull thud. A small dent appears in the body panel. He winces, pushes off the truck, and keeps fighting. The camera shakes from the impact. John glances at the lens and gestures a quick apology with a grin, then keeps fighting. A passerby stops and watches, pulling out a phone to film. Another passerby keeps walking, not interested. A guard takes a step forward, reaches for his radio, then stops, does not call. Someone in the distance laughs when John misses a punch. A car slows on the road, the driver looking over, then honks and drives off. Everyone glances at the sound for a split second. Pigeons scatter. A dog barks and pulls on its leash. In the distance, a street cleaner sweeps, not paying attention. A student with headphones walks by without looking. Someone photographs the building, then turns at the noise.

The sun catches the lens from behind the fighters — backlight glows softly around their silhouettes, hair glowing, a controlled soft flare drifting across the frame without washing out the image. A cloud passes, the light shifts for two seconds, then returns. The shadow of the truck moves. A glare flashes off the wet asphalt and briefly blinds the lens. The camera keeps moving, shaking, hunting for focus, losing and catching it again.

The fight slows for a second. Alexander blocks a punch, laughs shortly, nods at John — good one. He wipes sweat from his forehead with the back of his hand. He steps toward the camera, breathing hard, wiping his mouth, and says in clear, native Russian, perfect pronunciation, natural intonation: «Отлично, вот так снимает камера Sony. Сейчас покажу вам, как снимает другая камера.» He is about to continue — but from behind, John leaps into the frame with a jumping spin kick. His foot hits Alexander in the head. Alexander is knocked out of frame, out of the shot. The camera jerks, loses focus, the frame tilts, then holds on the empty space where Alexander stood. John lands on his feet, breathing hard, looking down at where Alexander fell. He takes a step forward, as if to help. He looks directly at the camera for the first time — tired, a little stunned. The fight is over. The shot ends on the puddle, the wet asphalt, and John standing in the background, chest heaving. The wind keeps blowing across the empty space where Alexander stood, moving John's clothes and hair as he catches his breath. A second of silence, just the wind and the water. Someone laughs quietly off-screen. The camera slowly lowers, as if the arms holding it are finally tired.

note.title: Стиль-блок: Sony VENICE 2 + ZEISS Supreme Prime
bullets: Каркас тот же (формат, дубль, ручная камера, язык), а вот камера и картинка другие: shot on Sony VENICE 2 with ZEISS Supreme Prime lenses.

8.6K full-frame sensor, 16 stops of dynamic range, dual native ISO 800/3200, wide color gamut exceeding BT.2020: технические параметры сигнализируют «класс камеры». Мы не настраиваем ими картинку, а помогаем модели угадать, к какой технике относится кадр.

cool neutral tones, clean sharp image, high detail, modern digital look, minimal fine film-like grain instead of electronic noise: главный контраст с Кадром 1. Там были зерно, Kodak, teal-and-orange; здесь холодные нейтральные тона и «чистая цифра».
smooth creamy bokeh with natural fall-off, round highlights in out-of-focus areas, no busy background rendering: характер размытия. «No busy background» просит не рисовать шумное боке.

Абзац про покрытие линз. The lens coating controls light — when sunlight hits the glass, the flare is soft and restrained, never washing out the image. Contrast stays high even in backlight. В Кадре 1 блики были желанным эффектом, здесь они сдержанные: это особенность конкретных объективов, и её нужно прописать.

Дефекты оператора остались (focus hunting, autofocus that breathes, horizon slightly tilted), убраны mechanical zoom и портрет оператора. Цвет, стиль и дефекты работают вместе: чистая картинка + живая рука.

note.title: Правило про оператора и локация
bullets: Новый блок. The operator is never visible in frame — no hands, no body, no face. Every mention of the operator refers only to the behavior of the camera: when the operator moves, the frame moves; when the operator breathes, the camera shakes slightly; when the operator ducks or steps back, the camera drops or pulls back.

Это третий способ решения проблемы «оператор в кадре» после смены точки съёмки и запрета: объяснить модели, как читать слова об операторе. Дальше в тексте можно писать «дыхание», «споткнулся», «отдёрнулся» и не бояться, что появится человек.

note.title: Свет и финал
bullets: The sun catches the lens from behind the fighters — backlight glows softly around their silhouettes… a controlled soft flare drifting across the frame without washing out the image: свет согласован со стиль-блоком (сдержанные блики).

Финал как шутка: Alexander объявляет «покажу, как снимает другая камера», и в этот момент John прыгает с вертушкой и выбивает его из кадра. Кадр holds on the empty space where Alexander stood, потом John смотрит в объектив, наступает секунда тишины, слышен смех за кадром.
He looks directly at the camera for the first time: взгляд в камеру как эмоциональная точка. До этого герои её «игнорировали».
Реплика 5 («Сейчас покажу вам, как снимает другая камера») сшивает кадр со следующим. Похожий финал повторится в Кадре 3: приём «рифмы» между кадрами.
